subject: WebMCPify Core
object: an MIT-licensed TypeScript ESM CLI, confined stdio MCP server, and optional Temporal worker for creating and verifying WebMCP capabilities; README roadmap identifies opt-in agent request/action analytics with success, rejection, failure and timing visibility as planned rather than implemented, with owner database integration and a potential free Improvisus Analytics destination subject to future availability/terms and owner-controlled redaction/retention, without automatic private-data upload

subject: The normal Core workflow
object: discovers first, accepts optional non-authoritative product context, then security check, human review, approved apply, browser test, and independent verification; review permits tool selection only, with read-only contracts/tasks, collapsible sections, patch-file reasons, and source consent cleared/disabled on partial selection; rejecting tools directly removes independent inline JS/TS registrations using a lazily loaded parser in a disposable workspace, preserves ordinary app handlers and exact unaffected task IDs/setup/outcomes/criteria, drops rejected-only and mixed/dependent tasks, and regenerates retained-only docs; ambiguous/shared source or TypeScript unused-integration cleanup uses a focused coding provider, while missing retained-tool coverage or test-count shortfalls use a source-frozen task-only pass; initial and revised drafts target 30 percent extra scenarios and require at least ceil(tool count times 1.2) valid tasks (the requested 20 percent lower bound) without a six-task ceiling, with every tool covered and extra unaffected tests preserved; providers may return only new-ID supplements, which Core merges with immutable retained tasks before validating the combined count and coverage; explicit TASKS_JSON blocks take precedence over unrelated examples; approved legacy sets remain readable and repair reviews (including durable repair) preserve fixed approved contracts/tasks; initial full durable review permits tool selection; all revised drafts undergo build/wiring/feedback/security and source/patch identity checks before fresh human approval; one review server locks controls across tabs/refreshes, reports progress, reopens revised drafts, supports repeated removals and failed-provider retry with selections retained, and drains finalized connections after response flush; target URL must be provided or set through WEBMCPIFY_URL; invalid verification tasks can be discarded only if the resulting count contract and tool coverage still hold; success tasks declare multi-tool setup; grounded rejection tasks preserve the unmet prerequisite and require observed tool/error evidence plus independent unchanged-state verification; source-only diagnostics use a dedicated source-edit prompt and one provider call with no schema or downstream validation, retain a private unapproved checkpoint and preserve existing target state; detailed generation/provider trace labels, event types and stream byte counts are opt-in via WEBMCPIFY_TRACE=1 and never expose prompts, source, tool arguments or raw provider diagnostics; diagnostic and metadata continuation flags belong to standalone generate rather than the full run workflow; pre-review generation and selected-tool revision aggregate missing/unprovable toolautosubmit attributes with form feedback failures, using confined source parsing to match HTML or JSX forms and static React attribute spreads while rejecting type/comment-only flags, unrelated forms and React boolean custom props; generation instructs safe unattended filters/search to emit an empty-string attribute and preserve actual SubmitEvent results, never bypassing required human confirmation or auto-editing sensitive forms to satisfy tests; requiredTools is an ordered call sequence that preserves repeated names and the final primary action through normalization, metadata correction, retained/new merging, approval storage and recorded execution scoring; existing canonical approvals remain unchanged and readable

subject: Generated source changes
object: a disposable workspace and reach the target only as an exact human-approved patch; Git check/apply consume the validated in-memory bytes via stdin instead of reopening a mutable pending path after hash checks; root/nested Serena state, dependency directories and .pnpm-store caches are excluded from workspace copies and captured patches even when force-staged, and patches targeting them are rejected without changing owner configuration; internal relative/absolute file and directory symlinks stay inside the copied snapshot, symlinked target roots are canonicalized, safe dangling links are preserved, and external source links fail with common-root guidance instead of exposing owner files; generation preserves JS/TS conventions, checks declarative form styling/status markers and collects all missing loaded CSS, per-form accessible status regions and activation/submit feedback into one component-targeted private report for the bounded source repair, and merges one root AGENTS.md combining repository instructions and detailed site capabilities with Improvisus/WebMCPify attribution; no second .agent.md is generated; root-served llms.txt/webmcp.md, static HTML capability guidance with truthful WebPage metadata, and scoped robots allowances are added when deployment is identifiable, separate from private run state; owner HTML/sections and crawler restrictions survive, README explains proposed capabilities, and an always-present deployment/GEO/AEO checklist covers real links/canonical/sitemap and search-versus-training controls without invented domains or indexing guarantees; wiring checks inspect current runtime files, not documentation or removed diff lines; preflight runs both declared typecheck/build scripts even when typecheck mentions build, runs dependency-free JS checks without node_modules, rejects unreadable/malformed package JSON or script/dependency maps as environment failures, anchors package-manager paths, skips stale optional dependency links, disables pnpm automatic before-run installs only in validation subprocesses without purging linked target dependencies, and distinguishes missing executables or interactive-install environment failures from source validation while safely naming the failed check; owned validation process trees stop before failed apply/build or cancellation rollback of patch paths, restoring originals/deletions/renames and removing newly introduced files using in-memory pre-apply classification unaffected by altered manifests; missing original backups never cause deletion of current source, other recoverable paths are still restored, and incomplete recovery retains evidence; post-success backup cleanup failure warns rather than rolling back; later browser failures, databases, payments, and arbitrary build side effects are not automatically undone; generation preflight and approved apply/typecheck/build disable pnpm before-run automatic dependency installation, preserving installed dependency trees and lockfiles outside source rollback coverage; normal generation separates compact source editing from read-only tool-contract and task authoring without a combined response schema, with existing source-mapped coverage accounting and bounded report/completion only where needed; metadata authoring freezes source and Git identity and retains provenance; a private unapproved source checkpoint precedes metadata, source-only diagnostics capture it and Git-identity-checked metadata-only diagnostics replay it exclusively in a disposable copy without a source provider, invalidating approval state, downstream checks, review or apply; malformed tools remain owned by bounded correction and checkpoints survive metadata failure; explicit completed-metadata continuation validates target/source provenance and confines artifact paths, freezes saved metadata in a new private artifact, skips initial source/tool/task generation, publishes the exact checkpoint discovery inventory with the pending draft for review and later stages while diagnostic-only modes preserve existing discovery, and retains existing metadata/coverage/build/security gates plus human review without automatic approval or apply; drafting, edit retry, source repair and capability completion leave package installation and build/typecheck execution to Core rather than the provider; target dependencies are reused only for Core-owned preflight, absent dependencies or a missing local TypeScript compiler fail declared checks as actionable environment errors rather than silently skipping validation, while dependency-free JavaScript checks and projects with no build checks remain supported; patch parsing inspects a private temporary file with ignored stdin and a 30-second SIGKILL deadline while preserving valid bytes and cleaning private files; async source-identity and patch applicability Git checks have the same deadline, and timed-out identity checks fail closed instead of returning an empty identity

subject: Core security gating
object: balance by default for run, standalone generation, audits, and review fallback; standalone security --strict selects the strict audit policy and fails on blocking findings without changing an existing draft policy; review preserves explicitly recorded draft policies, and generate exposes balance|ignore|strict selection; balance checks high-impact actions and invalid cross-origin allowlists; strict reviews declared execution scope, input bounds, privacy, origins and applicable controls without imposing backend authorization or identity/replay/quota requirements on browser-local reversible UI state; backend mutations and consequential effects retain their applicable checks, and high-impact effects cannot bypass them through a UI label; every mode preserves exact-patch human approval; a narrowly parsed non-consequential browser-local Zustand setter can reach scope review despite a high-impact name, using validated generation/revision source or exact pending text hunks reconstructed only in memory; real/unknown calls, unsafe persistence, shadowed factories and external paths remain conservative, with subscriber/middleware/deployment limitations disclosed

subject: Browser verification
object: each approved task on its exact acted-on tab in a fresh context, preserving DOM/component state, cookies, session storage and navigation without resetting personal CDP authentication; Core owns mandatory Chrome DevTools MCP and provides a token-authenticated task gateway exposing only list_webmcp_tools and call_webmcp_tool, delegating to upstream execute_webmcp_tool; provider instructions match actual advertised base methods and schemas rather than a fixed namespace/prefix and allow metadata-only native tool catalog search/loading for deferred methods without granting other browser methods or servers, binding a unique tab marker and rejecting unapproved names, routing and scripts; it parses validated structured inventories or titled/untitled text page listings without trusting URLs in titles, checks exact task markers, honors pageId schemas including identity probes, and retains private failed-binding diagnostics; it honors Completed/Error statuses and structured business errors, restores surviving selection before closing a task context, and records actual discovery/ordered calls rather than reports or initially-true checks; read-only invocation/tool/input-correlated observation preserves guard exceptions omitted upstream, with a bounded wait for separate CDP message delivery, never directly invokes capabilities or borrows console errors; MCP timeouts close the owned connection before retries; expected rejection requires one matching primary business error plus independent unchanged-state verification through a bounded 500 ms settle window, with ordered successful setup tools before the final requiredTools primary action, exactly one recorded error overall, declared error-contract checks bound to that final tool, and successful same-tool setup allowed and no guarantee against all later side effects; new tasks require null-safe storage checks, approved criteria stay immutable, and every verification read has a deadline and operation cancellation; infrastructure/evidence/verifier failures do not authorize source repair, remaining unexecutable tasks are marked not run, failed standalone audits exit nonzero, and durable attempts share this boundary; full UI baselines are opt-in via test/final-eval --baseline (default off), run before WebMCP testing and before apply in fresh final evaluation, and standalone baseline is UI-only; test artifacts link baseline scores, eval shows per-task comparisons and only exact-run final summaries, and failed baseline execution cannot complete a comparison while low UI scores alone are valid; final-eval checkpoints record the baseline choice, and failed providers cannot pass page checks; repair apply checks source/build and records awaiting-test without fabricated improvement, while final-eval/durable flows replay actions; final-eval reuse requires current execution-policy stamps, matching URL/provider/mode and complete exact task/results, UI-only baselines, and current local Git source identity for WebMCP; source/task drift invalidates CLI/durable attempts and local snapshots do not attest remote deployments; access is revoked before scoring, per-task diagnostics log bridge initialization/catalog request counts and bounded method/capability identifiers with execution status, Codex attempted MCP calls are logged separately from independent bridge evidence, catalogs served do not prove model visibility, and prompts/arguments/results/tokens and raw diagnostics stay private, and provider tool allowlists are not a universal OS sandbox

subject: Target-owned run state
object: the target project's .webmcpify directory, including discovery, proposals, approvals, approved tasks.json, security reports, patches, evaluations, rollback, and trajectories; standalone persistent discovery and fresh generation initialize a root /.webmcpify/ Git ignore rule immediately, creating a missing .gitignore, preserving owner rules/line endings and regenerating idempotently, before generation records its source baseline; this explicit housekeeping change is separate from exact human approval of application integration; metadata-only/continuation and preserve-approval generation do not rewrite existing source identity, and existing tracked files are not automatically untracked; ignored state remains readable by CLI and Temporal, source identity excludes runtime artifacts, and the owner must separately exclude them from deployment and protect retained private evidence; Git with a target HEAD remains required for reviewed source patches, not for tracking runtime state; the combined root AGENTS.md and served llms.txt/webmcp.md are separate reviewed public guidance files; all new task writes target .webmcpify/tasks.json, while a legacy root tasks.json is readable only when the private file is absent and must retain exact approval fingerprints; malformed or changed private criteria never fall back to root data, no legacy owner file is automatically removed, and baseline/Temporal metadata records the actual read path

subject: Temporal
object: optional and lazily loaded for full durable run, targeted repair and final evaluation; normal CLI/MCP paths work without peers; run --durable checkpoints discovery, generation/preflight, recorded security policy, initial tool-selection review, optional pre-apply UI baseline, exact approved apply/build, each approved WebMCP task and evaluation; stable canonical-target workflow IDs refuse duplicate active pipelines and execution IDs pin reattachment, which reports saved rather than fresh results for completed runs and surfaces the recorded failed phase plus fixed-text provider guidance without printing arbitrary Temporal causes; activities bind draft/policy/task/source identities, serialize shared worker state, heartbeat, carry local deadlines and propagate cancellation to provider and owned validation process trees before rollback; ordinary provider defaults remain unchanged while durable defaults use remaining activity time; automatic side-effect retries remain disabled and explicit repair budgets/frozen task criteria remain; new activity results keep source/task expressions/raw provider output local, but product-context inputs are history and must contain no secrets; final evaluation checks optional client availability and connection settings before browser/generation work, owns browser cleanup and saves reviewed checkpoint identity before baseline execution; final evaluation rejects incomplete task results or unusable UI baselines while allowing legitimate low UI scores, and retests all tasks after source-changing Temporal repair; isolated real-service fixtures cover heartbeat/cancellation, completed-stage restart, current/legacy replay and actual Core worker/Chrome execution with credential-free providers; approval remains a local activity and arbitrary in-flight crash recovery, production authentication and native Windows/macOS behavior are not certified; durable repair resolves the initiating CLI's canonical configured/selected provider and records it in workflow history rather than adopting a worker default

subject: Core development
object: strict TypeScript with NodeNext ESM, Node 20.19+ compatibility, pnpm, focused verification scripts, and the validation checklist in CONTRIBUTING.md

subject: Core security analysis
object: backend enforcement; universal provider attestation and production policy storage adapters remain unimplemented

subject: WebMCP and browser support
object: experimental and runtime-dependent, so availability must be detected rather than assumed

subject: Project memory
object: Barry Cache docs/context facts and ADRs; .codex project memory is retired and Serena remains a semantic code-navigation tool

subject: Provider generation
object: a provider-neutral output normalizer for raw text, JSON envelopes, JSONL events, nested assistant content, and future common response shapes; AGY uses accept-edits mode plus one edit-only retry for a text-only proposal; malformed tool/task metadata gets one metadata-only correction with source/Git identity and already-valid contract preservation, revalidation, and a canonical corrected review draft; valid contracts are retained for tasks-only corrections, which must return actual JSON rather than commentary and satisfy the existing coverage/count rules; concrete rejection errors may match a declared single-placeholder template without evaluating expressions, while runtime evidence still requires the approved concrete error; failed corrections stop before publishing a pending proposal; provider executable paths are anchored before workspace changes, Codex has standalone/editor fallbacks, and safe launch errors distinguish missing executables, working directories, and interpreters while keeping raw diagnostics private; Codex terminal error events produce fixed-text model-access, usage/capacity, authentication and connection guidance without printing raw messages, identifiers, prompts or code, interpreting echoed argv/warning items as failures, or changing provider settings; metadata/capability-completion and selection-revision wrappers preserve only this fixed guidance rather than hiding the actionable provider cause; explicit terminal Codex/Claude failure envelopes fail even with a zero process exit, while recovered turns remain valid; fixed-text provider timeout guidance survives metadata and coverage wrappers

subject: Source action discovery and generation completeness
object: uncapped discovery signal lists and deterministic lazily parsed JS/TS/JSX candidates for named handlers/store actions, conditional branches, and multiline callbacks; unresolved references remain source-inspection hints and parse failures retain regex signals with warnings; generation has no fixed tool-count limit and accounts for resolved candidates using exact declared handler matches or CAPABILITY_COVERAGE_JSON mapping to proposed tools, discovered existing registrations, or explicit source-grounded omission reasons, never arbitrary count/budget skips; unaccounted actions get one source-capable completion in the disposable workspace, preserving existing valid contracts and Git identity, requiring source edits for added tools, and revalidating scaled tasks, wiring, build, security, and human approval; explicit omissions survive metadata-only correction in the reviewed draft; dynamic/aliased/non-JS handlers and declared coverage still require agent inspection and runtime verification, so static discovery is not an exhaustive proof; owner-rejected review selections are not globally recompleted; labelled fenced/plain JSON or a single unambiguous unlabelled report object/fence normalize source-grounded current-draft existing labels to proposed, omit known unresolved hints from required accounting, and allow one report-only correction with source/Git identity and retained tools/tasks preserved; normalized coverage is included first in the reviewed draft and arbitrary unknown IDs, false mappings, unsupported existing claims and arbitrary omissions remain invalid; missing presentation headings do not require another model call or invalidate an otherwise source-checked report, while multiple unlabelled reports are refused as ambiguous; a proposed report entry can normalize a unique one-character 20-hex candidate-ID substitution or omitted final character only when a unique named handler in the reason and every referenced tool source file ground the same resolved candidate, with duplicate/ambiguous mappings still rejected and no extra model call for that normalization; Codex initial generation requests a closed structured final-response envelope containing complete JSON strings for tools/tasks and a native closed coverage object restricted to resolved discovery IDs to prevent missing inner JSON delimiters or invented IDs, normalized through the same domain validators; an absent report with uncovered actions gets read-only accounting before source completion, and failed report-only validation retains the original missing-action assessment rather than approving invented report mappings, while source/Git drift remains fatal; proposal instructions distinguish underlying application handlers from registration placement for effect inspection and require WebMCP JSX attributes to compile with local target typings without disabling checks; before preflight, identical repeated named imports are removed only from changed confined disposable source files, preserving type/value distinctions, comments, unusual imports and conflicting bindings, followed by ordinary compile/security and exact source review

subject: Disposable source workspace copying
object: Node fs.cp with optional COPYFILE_FICLONE, allowing native ordinary-copy fallback on unsupported platforms/filesystems and cross-device copies without source hard links; the existing nested .git/.webmcpify/.serena/node_modules exclusions are unchanged; copies reflect saved on-disk dirty/staged/untracked and required ignored files rather than a Git-only snapshot, while unsaved editor buffers cannot be copied; copying errors clean the partial temporary directory and propagate, and build validation, patch capture, approval, and cleanup behavior remain unchanged; actual speed/disk savings are filesystem-dependent, and no additional cache/build exclusions or custom parallel copier are introduced; source roots and returned workspace paths resolve OS directory aliases, and link confinement canonicalizes existing ancestors of dangling targets so macOS /var and /private/var spellings do not falsely appear external while external targets remain refused

subject: Hosted runtime compatibility checks
object: GitHub Actions runs Node 20 and 22 on Linux, macOS and Windows with browser-state checks retained; Linux allows user namespaces for only the installed Chrome executable via AppArmor; Windows grants AppContainer/LPAC read/execute access only to the downloaded Chrome installation; neither disables Chrome sandboxing; Execa 9.6 supports the declared Node 20 engine, and provider fixtures use executable Node shebang scripts instead of Windows cmd wrappers, with multiline/quoted/metacharacter/empty arguments tested; macOS CI restores the downloaded Chrome directory to a .app bundle before launch; missing explicit provider and validation executable paths are classified from filesystem evidence even when Windows supplies no ENOENT code, without exposing raw stderr or blaming generated source

subject: Codex MCP CLI override keys
object: unquoted server and environment key segments using letters, numbers, underscores or hyphens; dotted or quoted keys fail before provider spawn with a safe visible configuration error rather than silently configuring nested or literally quoted servers; mandatory WebMCP gateway settings retain required/enabled/tool allowlist overrides
